title: Microfix heuristics pocket digest
content:
Purpose: quick, grab-and-go heuristics for tiny, recurring edge cases we keep re-labelling. Not canonical — meant for single-session correction passes and pair-adjudication.

1) Slash-separated tokens ("/", "|")
 - If token is a compact identifier (e.g., 123/456) and both sides are numeric: treat as a single ID span.
 - If two words (e.g., "apple/orange") that are semantic alternatives: label as SINGLE span with tag=CHOICE only when downstream expects alternatives; otherwise split into two spans with relation LINKED.
 - URLs: never split on "/" inside domain/path; only highlight full URL.

2) Parenthetical disambiguators
 - "Widget (v2)" -> primary span = "Widget", qualifier =ANNOTATION:VERSION in metadata. If guideline requires single label field, include qualifier inside parentheses only when it changes meaning (e.g., model names).

3) Dates and incomplete timestamps
 - "03/24" ambiguous -> if context contains year -> resolve to MM/YY; otherwise mark as PARTIAL_DATE and add note.
 - "Mar 24" -> treat as month+day; if year absent, assume present-year only for user-facing logs, DO NOT normalize for training samples.

4) Emojis and reactions
 - Inline emoji used as sentiment cue (👍, 👎, ❤️): label as SENTIMENT_SHORT only when they change label decision. Otherwise ignore for entity spans.

5) Currency + ranges
 - "$5-$10" -> label as RANGE with two subspans: LOW="$5" HIGH="$10". For single-price heuristics prefer unified RANGE tag.

6) Abbreviations vs acronyms
 - If token all-caps length <=4 and appears in upstream glossary -> tag as ACRONYM. Otherwise annotate as ABBREV and add suggestion to glossary queue.

7) URLs: path vs query params
 - Highlight base path and hostname as PRIMARY_RESOURCE. Query params should not be labeled unless they represent a meaningful business entity (e.g., orderId=). If labeling query args, use SUBFIELD role.

8) Split-or-merge decision (short checklist for adjudicators)
 - Merge if: tokens are part of single canonical name (product codes, full names with initials).
 - Split if: tokens are independent items in enumerations or separated by conjunctions.

9) PII borderline (phone-like numbers <7 digits)
 - If context suggests local phone -> mark REVIEW. If clearly a model number or SKU, tag as PRODUCT_ID and add rationale.

10) Confidence and abstain buckets (fast heuristic)
 - Auto-abstain if: model-confidence <0.25 OR conflicting annotator labels >2.
 - Low-confidence flag: 0.25-0.5 (human double-check).
 - High-confidence: >0.75 (single-pass OK).

Quick examples (adjudicator shorthand):
 - "ACME-5/2023" -> PRODUCT_DATE (treat slash as part of id)
 - "Paris/London flights" -> SPLIT: two cities
 - "signup?ref=partner123" -> PRIMARY_RESOURCE=signup, SUBFIELD=ref (if label reqd)
 - "Dr. J. Smith" -> merge as PERSON; keep initials with surname

Notes to self / TODOs:
 - Run a 500-sample audit to catch aggression of RANGE merge heuristic (ticket JIRA-LAB-452).
 - Propose small update to labeling UI: checkbox for "preserve parentheses as qualifier" so adjudicators can mark quickly.
 - Add column to sample export: "heuristic_applied" for downstream model training traceability.
 - Check PR #87 for tokenizer changes that affect slash-splitting.

Open questions (for pair-review):
 - Should we ever normalize year-less dates to a canonical ISO for embeddings? Pros: consistent signals. Cons: injects false certainty. Leaning toward NO for now.
 - How often do emoji-semantics flip entity labels? Need a 1k-sample probe.

Scratch shorthand (for quick labelers):
 - "merge?" = likely same entity; "split?" = enumerated list; "abstain*" = unclear/multiple possible interpretations.

Slack refs: #labeling-help thread: recent convo re: slash-handling (see thread date 2024-01-22).

Bottom line: keep heuristics small, opinionated, and reversible. Prefer marking REVIEW over making potentially irreversible normalization in training data. Capture rationale in sample metadata every time a heuristic is applied.

Signed-off-by: Aisha (quick personal pocket guide)
